role_permission_map: 69 grants: pasien 13, dokter 16, apoteker 6, admin 10, superadmin all 24. Built with one rule - grant a permission to a role only where the plan names that role as a consumer of the action, or where the action is intrinsic to that role's own data - and every row cites its reason in RbacSeeder's docblock. The per-role highlights: pasien holds no clinical WRITE (may read its own record, may not write one); dokter holds the consultation lifecycle, the SOAP record write, e-prescription and medical letters, plus booking.batal because todo 27 records dibatalkan_oleh from users.tipe so a doctor cancelling yields 'dokter'; apoteker holds resep.verifikasi (todo 39 pharmacist-only) and NOT obat.cari (finding 3); admin holds promo.validasi, pdp.kelola and audit.lihat but NO rekam_medis.*, NO resep.buat and NO konsultasi.*, because todo 47's own acceptance criterion argues that widening audit.lihat "widens the blast radius", so it goes to no role that also holds a clinical write. superadmin is written out in full rather than computed, so the seeded table IS the policy.
no_superadmin_bypass_in_code: No code path anywhere grants everything to a role name. A hidden bypass would make every permission revocable in name only - audit.lihat would look granted in role_permissions and be un-revocable in the middleware - and would put a security policy in code where a data change cannot reach it. Two tests assert superadmin holds the whole catalogue: one against the constant, one reading the live rows back through the same join the middleware uses.
unknown_value_is_500_never_403: permission: with a code outside the catalogue, or tipe: with a value outside the ENUM, throws a LogicException and renders 500. A 403 would present a typo as an authorisation decision about a real user and point the investigation at the wrong file, and would deny EVERY caller forever while blaming the caller's token. Three tests pin this, including permission:booking.create and tipe:doktor.
permission_check_is_one_query: SELECT EXISTS over role_permissions joined to user_roles and permissions, one IN list, no per-role loop, and NO eager loading anywhere because the question is a boolean and there is no collection to load into. Proven rather than asserted: one test gives the caller all FIVE roles and 69 grants and counts with DB::listen requiring <= 2 queries, and a second requires the same bound for a caller with zero roles so a revoked account cannot take a different code path.
error_shape: | situation | status | body |.  anonymous (with or without auth:sanctum) -> 401 {"success":false,"message":"Unauthenticated.","errors":{}}; missing grant or wrong tipe -> 403 {"success":false,"message":"This action is unauthorized.","errors":{}}; unknown code -> 500 {"success":false,"message":"Internal server error.","errors":{}}. Both strings are byte-identical to bootstrap/app.php's exception renderer, asserted on the RAW body, so a client cannot tell which layer denied it. The responses are returned rather than thrown because a thrown AuthenticationException is rendered by shouldRenderJsonWhen(), which is false off api/* - returning makes the body path-independent. Every test asserts Location is absent; nothing redirects.

task: 20. Implement Module 1 auth endpoints: register, login, OTP verify, refresh, logout, devices
scope: 23 files: 8 new in app/Services/Auth, 1 controller, 7 FormRequests, 3 ApiResources, 2 test files; routes/api.php and app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php modified. 8 routes registered.
endpoints: POST /api/v1/auth/register (throttle:auth-otp-send 10/min) | POST /api/v1/auth/login (throttle:auth-login 5/min) | POST /api/v1/auth/otp/verify (throttle:auth-otp-verify 5/min) | POST /api/v1/auth/refresh | POST /api/v1/auth/logout (auth:sanctum) | GET /api/v1/auth/devices (auth:sanctum) | POST /api/v1/auth/devices (auth:sanctum) | DELETE /api/v1/auth/devices/{deviceId} (auth:sanctum)
RBAC_JUSTIFICATION: ZERO permission: and ZERO tipe: middleware on all 8 routes, decided against RbacCatalog::PERMISSIONS read in full. The 24-code catalogue names NO auth, session, token or device action; the closest are notifikasi.lihat and dokter.lihat. permission:notifikasi.lihat on POST /auth/devices would make a push REGISTRATION a READ permission and would permanently lock out perawat and kurir, which RbacCatalog documents as real users.tipe ENUM values holding no role and therefore no grant. tipe: on logout would lock every account type out of ending its own session. EnsurePermission and EnsureUserType throw LogicException (500) for an unknown code, and todo 4 forbids inventing permissions no route consumes, so the authenticated routes use auth:sanctum plus explicit user_id ownership scoping in SQL. A test parses routes/api.php and asserts every permission:/tipe: string resolves against RbacCatalog AND that the match set is empty, so todo 21 cannot introduce an unknown code and get a 500 at runtime.
OTP_FLOW: 6-digit random_int zero-padded code, only hash(sha256) stored (kode_hash is 64 chars, asserted != plaintext and == hash(plaintext)); kedaluwarsa_at = now()+5min; issuing supersedes prior unused OTPs for the same (user_id,tujuan) by setting kedaluwarsa_at = now(), because the DDL has no dibatalkan_at - so a superseded code fails through the SAME expiry branch, one rule not two. consume() selects candidates FOR UPDATE inside a transaction and only then reads sudah_dipakai, closing the double-verification race; it matches by hash_equals across ALL rows rather than only unused ones so replay, expiry and wrong-code stay distinguishable. Three rejections, all 422 with errors.kode. Plaintext leaves the process only through IssuedOtp::plainTextForClient(), which returns null unless app()->environment(local) - phpunit.xml sets APP_ENV=testing so the suite runs the REFUSING branch.
REFRESH_ROTATION: user_refresh_tokens row matching hash(sha256, presented) is selected FOR UPDATE before dicabut is read; then dicabut=1 and a new pair is issued. Replaying a spent token revokes EVERY live refresh token for that account and answers 401, because the schema has NO device_id column so no narrower correct action exists; per-device token revocation is recorded as impossible. All three rejection reasons share one client-facing string so the 401 is not an oracle. Access TTL reads config(sanctum.expiration)=1440 with a fallback so a future null cannot reopen the never-expire hole; refresh TTL 30 days; secret Str::random(80) stored only as SHA-256. Logout also deletes the Sanctum access token and sets user_devices.aktif=0 for every row of the account.

OWNERSHIP_RULE: One class, app/Services/Pasien/PasienRecordAccess.php, and every call site in PasienController is one of five statements: ownPasien(user) -> Pasien::where('user_id',$user->id)->first() or 403; then Child::whereBelongsTo($pasien) as the FIRST thing on every query; then a row addressed by {id} that is not found under that scope -> 404. Decidable because telemedicine_test.sql:220 is user_id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL UNIQUE, so at most one pasien row names a users row. whereBelongsTo is the explicit form (vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Eloquent/Concerns/QueriesRelationships.php:735) so the tenant filter is visible in one place and future code that queries pasien_alergi directly is visibly the odd one out.
403_VS_404_TENSION_RESOLVED_AND_REPORTED: The brief asked for cross-patient 403; the plan's todo 21 acceptance criterion demands 404 'so existence is not leaked across tenants'. BOTH implemented with the split explicit: row-addressed access to another patient's row is 404 (body byte-identical to a row that never existed, and the other patient's row read back unchanged); 403 is the capability refusal for a non-patient account - including a superadmin holding all 24 permission codes - and for a paciente account with no pasien row. A literal 403-for-another-patient's-row would be a cross-tenant existence oracle and is refused as a criterion. Both statuses tested on all seven mutating endpoints.
RBAC_JUSTIFICATION: Zero permission: and zero tipe:, decided against RbacCatalog::PERMISSIONS read in full. The 24 codes name booking, jadwal, konsultasi, rekam_medis, surat_keterangan, resep, obat, pesanan, pembayaran, promo, notifikasi, audit, pdp and dokter actions - none names a patient profile, a family member or an allergy, so any code here would be inventing policy (todo 4 forbids) and would require editing app/Support/Rbac/, which this todo may not touch. EnsurePermission throws LogicException (500) for an unknown code, so a typo is a build-time mistake rather than a 403. tipe:pasien WOULD resolve and is deliberately not used: it answers 'which account type is this', cannot express 'is this row yours', and a paciente account with no pasien row passes it and is refused by ownPasien() anyway. perawat and kurir are real users.tipe values holding no role, so any permission: is a permanent lockout for those two. Tripwire: PasienProfileTest re-parses routes/api.php and asserts every permission:/tipe: string resolves AND that the match set is empty.
APIRESPONSE_WIDENED: success() gained a 4th optional param ?array $meta = null, placed AFTER message so data stays between success and message as the mobile client and OpenAPI generator require. The key is OMITTED when null, never emitted as "meta": null, so every envelope the class has always produced stays byte-identical - which ApiKernelTest's exact-body assertion requires. Two derived helpers keep the key names in one place: pageMeta(LengthAwarePaginator) -> {current_page,last_page,per_page,total,from,to} and singlePageMeta(int) for a deliberately unpaginated list. MIGRATED: AuthController::devicesIndex moved from data:{devices,total} to data:{devices} + meta:{...}; the list is still one page (an account has a handful of devices) and is now reported as the degenerate single page it is so a client parses ONE list envelope. boundary_decisions: berlaku_sampai INCLUSIVE (a DATE has no time component, so the last moment of validity is the END of the date it names; the column is named "berlaku sampai" = valid through). | Slot step is mulai+durasi <= jam_selesai, so the window END is REACHABLE: 09:00-09:15 with a 15-minute duration offers exactly one slot. THE_REAL_BUG_THIS_TODO_FOUND_AND_IT_WAS_: Removing Fortify broke every unauthenticated API request. ApplicationBuilder::withMiddleware() registers a default guest redirect of fn () => route('login') at vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Foundation/Configuration/ApplicationBuilder.php:291, before the application's own callback runs, and Fortify was the only thing that made route('login') resolve. Without it, Illuminate\Auth\Middleware\Authenticate::redirectTo() at Authenticate.php:104 threw RouteNotFoundException, the middleware's own AuthenticationException was never thrown, the render callback in bootstrap/app.php never saw it, and an unauthenticated POST /api/v1/... returned a sanitised 500 where the contract promises 401. The fix is $middleware->redirectGuestsTo(null), the framework's own opt-out at Middleware.php:539, which installs fn () => null. It was caught by THREE TESTS THAT WERE GREEN AT THE BASELINE - ApiKernelTest::test_unauthenticated_request_renders_401_envelope_without_redirecting_to_login, ApiKernelTest::test_api_requests_render_json_even_without_an_accept_header and RbacMiddlewareTest's 401-envelope case - and by none of the eleven. Had the eleven been resolved by deleting the nine files and stopping, this would have shipped.

locking_strategy: One DB transaction. The FIRST statement is always a Dokter lockForUpdate, never jadwal first, because mixing scheduled and instant bookings would otherwise lock different rows and defeat the guard. The jadwal row is locked second when one is named. Capacity is a LOCKING CURRENT READ, that is a SELECT id FOR UPDATE counted in PHP, never an aggregate, because an aggregate takes no lock under REPEATABLE READ. Only UniqueConstraintViolationException retries, three nomor attempts inside the transaction then a 422; a 1205 lock timeout propagates rather than being retried.

B then receives a 1205 and after commit gets a SlotTakenException. Five alternating creates yield 1 row and 4 refusals. That is a CONVENTION: one spelling, no visibility of a relation traversal or a chunk(), defeatable by an author who does not know about it. Implemented instead a `retrieved` listener on RekamMedis and its four children, which Eloquent fires inside Model::newFromBuilder() - the ONE place every hydrated model comes from - so find, findOrFail, first, firstOrFail, chunk, cursor, lazy, lazyById, a lazy relation and a with() eager load ALL pass through it. Hydrating one of the five without an open RekamMedisReadScope throws. The grep is kept as a backstop and the DIFFERENCE IS MEASURED: mutation M1 removes the model event, the grep still passes, and two tests go red. Neither wall is asserted on the strength of the other.
NO_UNGUARDED_READ_PATH_HOW_IT_IS_PROVEN: Three walls. (1) RekamMedisReadScope::dalam() has exactly ONE caller in the application, RekamMedisAccessLogger::baca() plus its write sibling, and both have already INSERTed the log row in the SAME transaction; the order inside is fixed - a four-column DB::table() ownership probe that hydrates NOTHING and answers 403/404, then the INSERT, then the open. A rollback of the read takes the log row with it; a failed INSERT means the record is never hydrated. (2) Every public method of RekamMedisService takes a User and never a RekamMedis, so no caller can supply a record it opened itself. (3) The probe selects four named columns and the suite asserts the ownership triple, so it cannot be widened into a content read. THE RESIDUAL, STATED NOT HIDDEN: a non-hydrating query - RekamMedis::query()->pluck('subjektif'), ->value('plan'), ->exists() - fires no `retrieved` event and would return clinical content unlogged. No model-level guard can close it; closing it means intercepting every query at the connection layer, a global change this todo does not own. The service never does it and the probe is deliberately a projection rather than such a call.
WHAT_A_READ_IS_AND_EVERY_PER_CASE_COUNT: Defined as: every operation that OPENS an existing rekam_medis row or one of its four child tables AND COMPLETES writes EXACTLY ONE row. Measured: detail fetch 1 (patient, doctor, admin, superadmin); detail fetch with the chain 1, not 3; eager-loading the four children 1, not 5; a paginated list N (proven as N successive reads because the plan registers no list route); an edit of a draft 1; a finalisation 1; an amendment 1 (the PARENT is opened, the new row is created); a sub-entity write 1; a CREATE 0 (nothing pre-existing is opened and the log's five ENUM values are all read purposes, so there is no correct row); a 403 0; a 404 for another patient or an unrelated doctor 0; a 404 for a nonexistent id 0; a router 404 for a malformed id 0. THE ONE CASE THAT LEGITIMATELY WRITES TWO: a client retry is a second access, and collapsing it would make the log unable to answer 'was this looked at twice?'. Deduplication is impossible anyway - dibuat_at is a TIMESTAMP at one second of resolution, so the two rows are not even distinguishable by time, only by the auto-increment id. A record that is the parent of N amendments carries N rows, which is the same property from the other side.
A_REFUSED_WRITE_LOGS_ZERO_AND_THAT_IS_TH: The first implementation logged on the open and then threw, so a 422 rolled the log row back - the tests caught it and the rule was then STATED rather than patched. The log row and the operation share one transaction, so a refusal leaves no trace in either table. A log row for an edit that did not happen would be a false record, and a false record in an audit table is worse than a missing one. The obvious objection - that a 422 discloses status_dokumen - does not apply here because every refusal is reachable only by the record's OWN doctor, who already knows whether it is a draft. The disclosure that matters is a READ, and a read either completes and logs or never returns. the_dedupe_key_and_where_it_comes_from: (pembayaran.gateway, pembayaran.nomor_referensi). The gateway half is the {gateway} path segment, narrowed to the four ENUM members by a route whereIn compiled from PembayaranGateway::untukRute() - so the controller is unreachable for a segment outside them and the code that reads a secret never runs. The nomor_referensi half is minted by THIS application at initiation and echoed by the provider inside a body it SIGNED, so it is not free-form caller input. That is what makes an application-level key safe here: the usual reason to distrust one is that the client chooses it, and here we choose it and the provider attests it.
app_level_dedupe_no_index_added: NO index, NO constraint, NO column and NO migration was added, as the brief and the plan require. concurrency_analysis: SEQUENTIALLY exact: the first delivery leaves pending and the second sees a terminal status. CONCURRENTLY a real race exists and the schema cannot close it - two identical deliveries can both read pending before either writes. What closes it is PaymentService::huntap() issuing SELECT ... FROM pembayaran WHERE gateway = ? AND nomor_referensi = ? FOR UPDATE INSIDE the transaction: a locking read resolves against the LATEST COMMITTED version, so the second transaction blocks THERE, and when it unblocks it re-reads the now-terminal status and takes the duplicate branch. Proved with two genuine interleaved MySQL transactions on two connections at REPEATABLE READ with innodb_lock_wait_timeout=1: (1) the real PaymentService::terimaWebhook() collides and raises MySQL 1205 writing nothing; (2) a plain consistent read of the same row does NOT wait and returns pending, which is why the locking read is the defence rather than an optimisation; (3) a locking read issued after the first commit returns the settled status, not a snapshot. COST NOT HIDDEN: a FOR UPDATE whose predicate matches no index takes gap locks on the range it scans, so the statement is a full scan of pembayaran and two unrelated payments can briefly serialise behind each other - a throughput cost, not a correctness one, and the price of the DDL being read-only. INDEX (gateway, nomor_referensi) would turn the scan into a point probe; it is NOT added and is recorded instead.
invalid_signature_no_state_change: The load-bearing assertion is on STATEMENTS, not rows: DB::listen captures every query the forged request issues and the test requires ZERO of them naming pembayaran, invoice or booking. A handler that read a row and then rejected the signature would leave the rows unchanged too, so a no-state-change assertion would pass it - requiring zero statements cannot. Row-level assertions follow (status still pending, dibayar_at NULL, webhook_payload NULL, invoice still menunggu_pembayaran, lunas_at NULL, booking still menunggu_pembayaran, audit_log update count unchanged from 0). The endpoint is UNAUTHENTICATED by design (a payment provider holds no Sanctum token) and {gateway} is validated by the ROUTER before the controller, so the code that reads a secret is unreachable for a segment outside the ENUM.
signature_scheme: HMAC-SHA256 over the RAW REQUEST BODY (Request::getContent()), keyed by config(services.payment.gateways.{gateway}.webhook_secret), lowercase hex, compared with hash_equals, in header X-Payment-Signature. Verified BEFORE the body is parsed, so an unsigned request cannot choose its own error. Four DIFFERENT secrets, asserted pairwise distinct and each at least 32 characters; a body signed with doku key is refused on midtrans. A body re-serialised with one trailing space added is refused, which is what proves the HMAC is over the wire bytes and not over a re-encoding of a decoded array. The signature is computed IN THE TEST from config() rather than by asking the implementation to sign, so the test fails against any scheme the implementation chose including none.
webhook_payload_overwrite_decision: A re-delivery does NOT overwrite it. The column (:968) is the forensic record of the delivery that CAUSED the state change and there is exactly one of those; a retry carries no new information and letting it write would replace the evidence with a near-copy. It is STRUCTURAL rather than a policy - the duplicate branch returns before any assignment, so there is no line to get wrong. The test re-delivers a DIFFERENT byte sequence (percobaan 2 plus its own catatan key) and asserts the stored JSON still reads percobaan 1 with no catatan key. One caveat stated rather than hidden: MySQL native JSON NORMALISES on store (member order, insignificant whitespace), so the comparison is toEqualCanonicalizing and the honest claim is that every key survived with its value, not that the bytes round-trip.
three_counters_behind_exactly_one_state_: pembayaran declares NO diubah_at (:958-:973, only dibuat_at at :969), so two writes in one second are indistinguishable from one. The clock is frozen at 2026-03-11 10:00:00, the first delivery is made, the clock is ADVANCED one hour, the second is made - so any re-application writes different values. Counter 1 pembayaran.dibayar_at (:967) still the first instant; counter 2 invoice.lunas_at (:950) still the first instant; counter 3 audit_log update rows exactly 1/1/1 for pembayaran/invoice/booking, which is the only non-timestamp counter and catches a re-write landing on the same instant.
second_response_is_a_success_and_the_exa: The two decoded bodies are diffed RECURSIVELY and the difference set is required to be exactly ["data.duplicate", "message"] - the envelope key set, the key ORDER, the HTTP status (200 twice) and the content-type are all asserted identical, and success is true on both. message is the second legitimate difference and is a DECISION WITH A COST: a body saying "payment updated" about a delivery that changed nothing is a lie a provider log would preserve; the cost is that a client keying logic off message rather than off data.duplicate will misread a retry, and the envelope documents message as human-readable and data as machine-readable. The retry is a DIFFERENT byte sequence so the payload assertions are measurements rather than accidents of formatting.

how_oversell_is_prevented_without_a_uniq: DIRECT ANSWER, because "add a constraint" is the reflex and it is both forbidden and wrong. (1) Oversell is NOT a duplicate-row problem: a unique index forbids two rows with the same key, while oversell is a read-modify-write race on ONE row. No index shape expresses "this row must retain at least N units", because that is a property of a column VALUE AT WRITE TIME, not of a key uniqueness. (2) THE SERIALISATION POINT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY UNIQUE: uq_stok (apotek_id, obat_id) at 840 means exactly one row per (pharmacy, drug), which is what makes the pessimistic lock addressable. Every competing checkout of the same drug at the same pharmacy passes through the same row. NO NEW INDEX IS NEEDED AND NONE IS ADDED. (3) A hypothetical UNIQUE (apotek_id, obat_id, jumlah_stok) would forbid two PHARMACIES holding the same count rather than forbid overselling.
the_two_mechanisms_in_the_service: kurangi() is the ONLY writer of jumlah_stok in the whole application and it is two mechanisms that fail differently. (1) A LOCKING READ of one row, SELECT ... FROM apotek_stok WHERE apotek_id = ? AND obat_id = ? FOR UPDATE, never an aggregate: compileAggregate() drops the lock so ->count()->lockForUpdate() is a SILENT no-op, and under REPEATABLE READ a plain consistent read sees the transactions own snapshot while a locking read always observes the latest committed version. This is the BookingService idiom verbatim. (2) A CONDITIONAL WRITE that carries the predicate, UPDATE ... SET jumlah_stok = jumlah_stok - ? WHERE id = ? AND jumlah_stok >= ?, refusing when affected() is not 1, which makes a negative value UNREPRESENTABLE IN THE WRITE rather than merely unlikely and does not depend on the lock. Plus a DETERMINISTIC LOCK ORDER: apotek_stok rows are taken in ASCENDING obat_id, because two checkouts of the same two drugs whose resep_item rows are stored in opposite order would otherwise make InnoDB detect a cycle and roll one back with error 1213.
the_concurrent_oversell_test: ApotekStokConcurrencyTest with a REAL second PDO connection, not a mocked assertion that a lock method was called. Choreography: connection A begins, its first apotek_stok statement is the locking read, the QueryExecuted listener fires SYNCHRONOUSLY inside A, and connection B runs the REAL unmodified PesananObatService for a DIFFERENT patient and prescription but the SAME drug at the SAME pharmacy, with innodb_lock_wait_timeout set to 1. Two different prescriptions on purpose, because two patients racing for one prescription would contend on resep first and prove something else. The listener additionally filters on QueryExecuted::$bindings for the exact (apotek_id, obat_id) pair, so it cannot fire on a row B never asks for. Asserted in order: A committed an order and the shelf is 0; the listener fired; B threw and the driver code read out of QueryException::$errorInfo[1] is 1205, via a helper that walks getPrevious() because whether Laravel maps 1205 to DeadlockException is a framework detail; B wrote neither a pesanan_obat nor an invoice; after A commits B retries and is refused with a StokTidakCukupException naming "tersedia 0, diminta 1", which is what proves the availability decision is a CURRENT read; and THE HEADLINE, jumlah_stok is EXACTLY 0, never negative, with exactly one order existing. A sequential twin runs the 1-of-N criterion over HTTP: five checkouts for one unit give 1 success, 4 refusals, shelf 0.
the_control_for_the_oversell: And it is the reason the test above is worth reading. Same choreography with NEITHER mechanism: B reads the shelf with a plain consistent read, which takes NO locks, so it neither blocks A nor is blocked by A; the test asserts B snapshot still reads 1 AFTER A committed, which is what makes it a race rather than a sequence; B then runs an UNGUARDED write that is applied to the latest committed row and lands on zero, producing MINUS ONE, and WHERE jumlah_stok < 0 then finds exactly one row - the oversell report docs/schema-notes.md says the signed column exists to make possible. A separate test isolates the conditional write alone by calling the service with the row already at zero and no contention at all.
tracking_vocabulary_derived_from_the_ddl: pesanan_obat_tracking.status is VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL at 822 with no ENUM, no CHECK and no index, while SHARING A NAME with pesanan_obat.status, a six-value ENUM at 810-811. the_tracking_transitions: The map has EIGHT edges: four along the happy path plus dibatalkan from each of the four live states. menunggu_pembayaran -> diproses, dibatalkan; diproses -> siap, dibatalkan; siap -> sedang_dikirim, dibatalkan; sedang_dikirim -> selesai, dibatalkan; selesai and dibatalkan terminal. EVERY legal edge is driven, walking the order onto each FROM state through the real service first, and asserts the order moved, the trail grew by exactly ONE row, the new rows status/keterangan/lokasi are what was passed, and no earlier row was rewritten. EVERY illegal pair walks the FULL 6x6 = 36 matrix rather than a sample: 8 legal, 28 refused, each with two messages asserted by position and each leaving both the order status and the trail count untouched. Both terminals refuse all six targets. An unknown status is a DIFFERENT 422 naming the six values, raised before the map is consulted. no_resi is accepted on sedang_dikirim only, because a courier reference on a parcel that has not left is a fact about a shipment that has not happened.
the_read_direction_is_proved: pesanan_obat_tracking.status is writable by anything, so a test writes sedang_dikirim into the trail BEHIND the services back and asserts the API reports menunggu_pembayaran from pesanan_obat.status while publishing the trail as stored. The trail is a record, not a filter: a client that disagrees with itself is shown the disagreement rather than a sanitised version of it. This is the only way to prove the read direction, because the two are written in one transaction and can only be made to disagree by writing around the service.

mutation_harness_with_control_first: CONTROL FIRST, in three parts. (1) A PARSER SELF-TEST on six synthetic reports, because the reporter is injected by the orchestrator, is NOT owned by this repository, and is NOT STABLE about the failed key: across green runs in this session it was observed both ABSENT and PRESENT as 0. So key presence cannot certify the parser and the harness feeds it green-with-absent, green-with-zero, red-with-one, red-with-errors-and-absent, red-with-a-lost-run and red-with-tests-absent, and requires the right verdict from each. All six correct. The verdict is a conjunction of result, failed, errors, tests === passed and tests > 0, so each conjunct closes a different hole. (2) THE CONTROL RUN RAN FIRST and was green: 50 tests, 768 assertions, failedKeyPresent false on that run; the key presence is RECORDED not ASSERTED, because of the instability. (3) An APPLY-CHECK: every mutation reports whether its search string was found, because a mutation that does not apply leaves the code untouched, the suite stays green, and the naive reading is SURVIVED, which is the wrong direction. Plus a PARSE-ERROR GUARD: a mutation that leaves the file unparseable errors every test, which looks like the strongest possible signal and measures nothing - the first draft of M6 did exactly that, scoring 32 failed and 6 errors from an unbalanced brace, and was rewritten as a valid reversed sort. An out-of-band scan over 19 files agrees: 0 non-ASCII code points and 0 homoglyph hits across the Cyrillic, Greek, dash-like, quote-like, ellipsis, nbsp, minus-sign and multiplication-sign ranges. (2) THE TOKEN AUDIT, PER TABLE: the first draft scraped every backticked token from every authored file and 140 of the candidates were NOT schema tokens at all, because routes/api.php backticks class names, permission codes and route names and the test files backtick PHP methods - a gate that mostly measures its own noise is a gate nobody reads. So the audit is a DECLARED VOCABULARY checked against the projects own SqlSchemaParser, the same parser sehatly:verify-schema uses, PER TABLE, which is strictly stronger than a flat name set because jumlah_stok existing somewhere says nothing about apotek_stok having it. 71 declared columns across 11 tables, 0 unresolvable, and COMPLETENESS asserted for the three tables this todo writes. (3) CITATION BOUNDS: every :NNN against the DDLs 1349 lines; the negative lookbehind is load-bearing because without it the time portion of a frozen clock is a citation, and the first run reported ten of those and the second reported one more - the literal in the tests own comment, which is why the gate scans itself.
the_enum_value_bucket: Kept separate, per column, with toBe so ORDER is checked as well as membership: pesanan_obat.status 6, .tipe 3, .kurir 6, faskes.tipe 5. money_at_the_boundary: JSON strings everywhere: subtotal, biaya_kirim, total, harga_jual and every resep_item price. subtotal is RECOMPUTED as harga_satuan * jumlah and never read off resep_item.subtotal, because nothing checks that equality - no CHECK, no generated column, no trigger - so a stored figure nothing maintains can be wrong, and a test plants a deliberately wrong stored value and asserts the recomputed one. The order total is goods plus shipping and nothing else, because pesanan_obat has no admin-fee and no discount column, so anything else would be money this API cannot represent; the invoice has five money columns and is where a promo or a payment method changes the figure, and the two are asserted equal when neither is used. the_char16_finding: STATED PLAINLY: a 16-character column CANNOT hold ciphertext, so the schema change is UNAVOIDABLE and this todo did not write the migration - migrations are schema authority and a separate concern. Proved by the DATABASE, not argued: a real insert into the REAL patients.nik column carrying a real 88-character payload is refused by MySQL with driver code 1406, and the row count is unchanged, so it is a refusal and not a silent truncation. The same test then inserts the same payload into a CHAR(16) probe column (1406) and a TEXT probe column (stored, read back byte-identical). The arithmetic: 16 bytes of plaintext always pad up under PKCS#7, so AES-256-CBC yields 32 bytes of ciphertext, and the stored payload is 88 characters by DESIGN - 6 header (4 magic + 2 key id) + 16 IV + 32 ciphertext + 12 HMAC tag = 66 bytes = exactly 22 base64 groups, so no = is stored. The plans own rule at :58 - never encrypt a value into a column narrower than its ciphertext - makes CHAR(16) a self-contradiction in the declared schema.
proposed_migration_someone_must_author: ALTER TABLE patients ADD COLUMN nik_cipher TEXT NULL COMMENT AES-256-CBC payload, ADD COLUMN nik_index CHAR(16) NULL COMMENT HMAC-SHA-256 blind index of the plaintext, first 16 base64 characters, ADD UNIQUE KEY uq_patients_nik_index (nik_index). And ALTER TABLE patients_family_members ADD COLUMN nik_cipher TEXT NULL - the cipher column and NOT the index, because :263 carries no UNIQUE. The original columns STAY: readable, never written by the application, and the DDL UNIQUE on patients.nik is NOT dropped, so two UNIQUE constraints coexist and that is correct. the_hmac_index_unique_proof: EXECUTED IN SQL, not argued. One MySQL TEMPORARY table holds nik_cipher TEXT, nik_index CHAR(16) UNIQUE and a third column indexing the CIPHERTEXT DIGEST instead. ONE NIK, TWO payloads (random IV), ONE HMAC index: the second insert is REFUSED with driver code 1062. A THIRD insert of the SAME NIK indexed by the ciphertext digest is ADMITTED, and the table then holds two rows for one NIK. A DIFFERENT NIK is admitted, so the index is not so coarse that everything collides. A temporary table is reported by NEITHER information_schema.TABLES NOR information_schema.STATISTICS, which is asserted together with a row insert so the empty result cannot pass vacuously - that is how the experiment runs without a migration and leaves the parity verifier clean.
why_not_a_hash_of_the_ciphertext: The shortcut index = substr(hash(ciphertext),0,16) cannot work, and the table above is the reason: the payload carries a random IV, so one NIK has as many payloads as it has encryptions, their digests differ, UNIQUE does not fire, and the duplicate is admitted. The only way to make a ciphertext-derived index deterministic is to fix the IV, which turns the whole column into deterministic encryption and leaks equality everywhere the ciphertext is read - data file, binlog, backup, query log. Equality leakage is paid ONCE, in a column built for lookup, and not twice. Mutation M6 reintroduces the shortcut and is killed by 5 tests.
why_hmac_and_not_a_bare_digest: A bare digest of a 16-digit number is reproducible by brute force by anyone holding the column, and truncating to 16 characters does not change that - the NIK space is 10^16, which is enumerable. A test computes substr(base64_encode(hash(sha256,nik)),0,16) and asserts it is NOT the index, and asserts that a DIFFERENT NIK_CIPHER_KEY produces a different index, so the key is inside the MAC. A database-only leak - backup, replica, binlog, stolen dump - is therefore not enough to confirm a guessed identity. The width is 16 characters because 16 base64 characters carry 12 bytes, so 96 of the 256 HMAC bits survive; the expected birthday collision over 1.3e8 NIKs is on the order of 1e-11. Halving it to 8 would leave 48 bits, and mutation M4 does exactly that and is killed by 4 tests.
the_privacy_tradeoff_stated_honestly: The index is a BLIND INDEX and it is a real cost, not a free win. It makes equal NIKs LINKABLE: an observer holding the column can group rows and learn which patients share an identity, which in a telemedicine product reveals household and family structure and says which rows to correlate across tables. An observer holding the column AND the key can go further and CONFIRM a guessed NIK by recomputing one index, which turns the column from a grouping key into a confirmation oracle. That is why nothing in this design ever decrypts a row to answer does this NIK already exist, and why indexMatches() is the only comparison and uses hash_equals. It is acceptable HERE for one reason only: the DDL MANDATES UNIQUE on patients.nik, so deduplication is a stated integrity requirement that cannot be dropped for a nicer privacy property, and a registry that admits two rows for one person is a defect that propagates into every clinical record attached to that person. It is NOT acceptable on patients_family_members, which carries no UNIQUE: an index there would buy no integrity guarantee while still linking every relative of every patient, so that tables migration gets the cipher column and no index, and index() is an explicit call so the decision is visible at the call site.
key_source_missing_key_and_rotation: NIK_CIPHER_KEY in the environment, read by config/nik.php into nik.key. NOT APP_KEY and not derived from it: APP_KEY rotates for a suspected cookie compromise or a new deployment, and because the index is derived from the same secret that would re-derive every index, make the duplicate check report every NIK as untaken, and render clinical records unreadable - an unrelated security action becoming destructive. Mutation M10 points config/nik.php at APP_KEY and is killed by a test that re-requires the config file with a controlled $_ENV. A MISSING or wrong-shaped key raises MissingNikCipherKeyException on encrypt(), index() and decrypt() with a message naming the variable, saying base64 and 32, and giving the one-line command. The guard is DEMONSTRATED not asserted: openssl does NOT validate key length, and the test proves it accepts a 6-byte key and returns a well-formed 32-byte ciphertext, then proves NikCipher refuses it. A base64: prefix is accepted because that is Laravels own convention. ROTATION is a RE-ENCRYPTION PASS, not a config edit: the root key is expanded by hash_hkdf into THREE independent subkeys (cipher, index, MAC), every payload carries a two-byte key id derived from the cipher subkey, and NIK_CIPHER_PREVIOUS_KEYS lets decrypt() read rows written by any of them, so the new key deploys BEFORE the rows are rewritten. The suite proves a payload written under key A reads back under key B with A listed and is REFUSED with A absent. WHAT ROTATION BREAKS, stated rather than discovered: the index is re-derived, so until EVERY row is rewritten the uniqueness check reports a duplicate NIK as untaken - asserted directly, the old and new indexes differ and indexMatches against the old one is false under the new key. The MAC is verified under the key that WROTE the payload, not the key in force; checking it against the current key was a real bug the rotation test found, and it rejected every pre-rotation row, the exact opposite of what the previous-key list is for.
encrypt_then_mac_and_how_it_was_found: The first implementation was CBC plus a magic marker, a key id, a stored IV and a PKCS#7 padding check, and the suite found a real hole in it: a real payload whose 16-byte IV was zeroed was NOT refused - openssl_decrypt returned 17 bytes of plausible-looking garbage that PASSED the padding check. A masked NIK built from those bytes would have been served to a client as a real patient identifier. So the payload became ENCRYPT-THEN-MAC: a 12-byte HMAC-SHA-256 tag over the header, IV and ciphertext, verified with hash_equals BEFORE openssl_decrypt is called. The ordering is load-bearing; the other order is the padding oracle. The test does NOT assert the 1-in-256 event, because a 1-in-256 assertion is a flaky test; what it asserts is the property that removes the dice - one flipped tag bit and one flipped ciphertext bit are both refused, and both refusals are corrupt() rather than unknownKey(), which proves the header was read first and the tag second. The unique key spans THREE columns and disetujui is NOT NULL with no nullable twin, so a decision about a given document version is IMMUTABLE and the only representable revocation is a NEW versi_dokumen carrying disetujui=0. The effective consent is the row with the MAXIMUM versi_dokumen. IS A REVOCATION AT VERSION N UNDONE BY A CONSENT AT N-1? No, on two independent grounds: a version below the maximum is REFUSED at the door with 422, and even if it were written the read side takes the maximum, so a resurrected N-1 row is invisible and the client would be told withdrawn while its re-consent never lands. That is the defect the write-side guard exists to prevent, and mutation M2 below removes the guard to prove it. HIGHEST IS A STRING ORDER and this is stated rather than hidden: the column is VARCHAR(20) and the database is created COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci at :11-:13 with no per-table override, so v10 sorts BELOW v9 because 0x31 < 0x39 at the second position. There is no numeric column to cast, so the mitigation is a fixed-width or zero-padded writer convention documented in the PdpConsent class docblock, and the code does not paper over it. EVERY COMPARISON IS DONE IN SQL because the collation is case and accent insensitive: v1.0 and V1.0 are the same value to uq_consent but different strings to strcmp, so a PHP pre-check would disagree with the constraint and a client holding V1.0 against a stored v1.0 would pass strcmp and then be killed by a raw 1062. Equality is where(versi_dokumen, $versi) and ordering is where(versi_dokumen, >, $versi), both evaluated by MySQL in the same collation the constraint uses, so V1.0 is correctly a COLLISION. The three-state answer keeps null (no row ever recorded) distinct from false (a row says no), because a checklist that renders never-asked and asked-and-declined both as no cannot show a person what is on record about them.
